text:
Be aware of the “free trial” !. I was hanging out with my friend one day when she told me about this app, it looked like a useful tool to navigate my city for walking/biking so I decided to download it. Upon downloading, there was a pop up advertising their subscription plans. The options were weekly, monthly or annual but they also offered a month long free trial. I went with that just to get a feel of the app and if I’d really use it. 

After I clicked on free trial, I was asked to make a payment of $0.00 and on the very bottom it stated I would be charged by the end of this month. I “paid” them only to get a call from my bank less than 20 minutes later asking if the recent $85.59 charge was fraud. I wasn’t even aware Strava was trying to charge me so I told them to dispute it. I deleted my newly made account along with the app because it didn’t seem like a trustworthy platform, trying to charge me for an annual subscription when I simply wanted a free trial. 

I thought the issue was resolved until I tried to download a different app about a day later, and since there was a “pending charge” for Strava, there was some sort of lock on my account. I called Apple and they told me since I disputed it with my bank I’d have to pay the $85.59 and then request a refund. That seemed a little strange to me but I went ahead and did so. 

I’ve now requested a refund through Apple 2x and each time it’s been denied. I’ve reached out to Strava and it seems I keep getting automated responses that are no help. So now, I’m out $85.59 and I don’t even have anything to show for it since I deleted my account completely. 

I have never been scammed like this. I’m not sure how, but the Apple support assistant told me they could tell I only had the account for less than 2-3 hours and I did select free trial…but they charged me for a year long subscription. 

In my opinion, this app isn’t worth it. I feel so embarrassed and upset. If I had known in hindsight all of this would happen, I simply would’ve looked up a map of my city and circled the trails/paths I’d like to check out instead of going through all of this to get my money back.
title: Be aware of the “free trial” !

text:
Plus un réseau social qu’une app sportive.. Alors là … ça me dépasse complètement. 
On parle quand même d’une référence ULTRA connue dans tout le globe, Strava… 
Strava qui pendant très très longtemps ne permettait pas sur smartphone d’avoir son tracé et ses stats sur le même écran,  alors oui la nouvelle mise à jour est vraiment bien mais bordel, je n’arrive pas à comprendre comment une application dites « experte » dans le domaine sportif peut avoir un retard de technologie si important. 
Expliquez moi comment ils n’ont pas pensé à mettre une option pour verrouiller les commandes de l’écran du smartphone tout en laissant l’écran déverrouillé ce qui éviterai qu’une satanée goute de sueur arrête notre enregistrement en plein milieu de notre activité … 
Pour rappel, Strava est sorti en 2009 ! 
Non mais sérieusement, ils viennent tout juste de permettre d’avoir nos stats avec notre tracé sur le même écran, ils ont mit 16 ans à avoir l’idée ?! Ils n’ont toujours pas donné l’accès à un écran d’activité personnalisé, qu’on puisse choisir parmi 3-4 possibilités, les infos que l’on souhaite voir pendant notre séance ! Comment après 16 ans y’a pas un couillon qui s’est dit « ah bah, ça serait peut être sympa un petit bouton pour verrouiller les commandes » (comme l’appli Forme d’Apple fait depuis… 10 ans!) ?!
En fait c’est bien dommage, Strava est un réseau social, pas une application pour sportif.
title: Plus un réseau social qu’une app sportive.

text:
Want to love but a bit glitchy. Love the idea of this app! And with a few improvements, it could be perfect. For one, as other users have stated, it often creates and narrates unnecessary turns in the middle of the run. I will be on a straight section and it will say “turn right, turn left” to keep me going straight. Two, no matter how many times I select the option to only announce turns on my phones, the app will announce from my phone to my headphones AND watch app will announce for everyone nearby to hear. It’s incredibly annoying. Three, because of all the unnecessary audio cues, I often have to pull out my phone to check the map. It would be so much easier if one of the options on the watch app was a map zoomed in on my current location on the run. Four, I wish I could select how many announcements I want for turns. Sometimes it’s just one per turn, sometimes it feels like 3-4. It’s very disruptive. And last but certainly not least (maybe the most annoying glitch!), sometimes I need to pause my run to look at the map. Whether I pause from my watch or phone app, it will immediately “resume” on its own. So I’ll pause it again, then it will restart immediately, and on and on. I hate the impact that has on my mileage times since the app is tracking my pace / mileage. If you’re someone who likes to stop and stretch or stop and walk, this glitch might be a deal breaker. 

For the pros, it’s really easy to create and share new routes. I can also make them private which is great so strangers don’t know my routes. You can create routes using roads, trails, paths, etc. - anything that would show up on a map. If your trail run has a lot of turns, it gets pretty annoying with the constant interruptions but it’s better than having to carry my phone and check the map all the time. 

Honestly if they can fix the issues above, this will be my favorite running app. And until then, I’m still going to use it because I like to run different routes without having to stare at my phone the whole time and I have yet to find another app that does everything I want.
title: Want to love but a bit glitchy

text: Great App, Needs Some Improvements. I’ve been using RunGo for three years now and am a paid subscriber. Overall, this is a great app. It’s easy to create and save routes, audio cues work well and it syncs with Apple Health and Strava. I do wish they would make some improvements. When you create a route, at each point you add it often adds unnecessary turns. For example, if I add a point on a straightaway, it will sometimes say, “turn left, now turn right” or “turn around, turn around”. Trying to edit these points often messes up the entire route. For detailed editing and certain features, you need to use a computer. Also, Facebook login no longer works correctly and it took over a week for support to migrate my login. Lastly, if you go off route (which is easy to do when trail running) it won’t let you know for over a 10th of a mile, so it ends up adding about a quarter mile to the run if you have to backtrack. All this said, this has become a vital running app for me and it has many powerful features that don’t seem to exist in any other running app. It filled the gaps that Strava’s routes lack, and if you already have routes in Strava you can import and manipulate them in RunGo. For what it can do, it definitely deserves 4 stars.

text: TikTok wannabe. This app is so useful for biking navigation that it is tragic that the entire experience is locked behind an idiotic UI designed to “engage” users over the utility it otherwise provides. I have no desire to use a navigation app as a social media tool and I deeply resent the developers’ insistence that I should. For example, you need to dig deep to uncover the actual navigation utility of the app. When you go to plan a route for the day you actually have to switch the command interface off it’s default setting, which is designed to let you “discover” routes nearby, rather than actually routing you to your destination; to do that, you have to press the “+ Plan” button. Ridiculous. Also, there is no clear way to end a route once you are finished with it. To do this you have to go into the “controls” button and then press a “Pause” button and then there are about 5 more pop up screens you have to click through to actually end the route. For a paid app, this is an absurd amount of effort to go through for basic functionality. I DO NOT WANT to use a navigation tool as a social media bit. I suggest the developers bifurcate the navigation tools from their attempt to be the TikTok of biking. Not every app needs to be a social media engagement platform. Stop this nonsense/ you are not TikTok and you never will be. Stay in your lane
title: TikTok wannabe

text:
Don’t spend your money. I needed a simple route planner for my custom rides. I don’t want to share the routes with anyone else. It’s a pain to go into settings to make everything private. Privacy should be the default since I’d rather my address (starting point) NOT be shared with everyone. 

When making rides that start and end at the same point, this app has a stroke if the custom waypoints cross previous sections of the route. If I’m selecting, let’s say, waypoint 9 of my ride, and I try to cross an earlier section in the path, it’ll keep resetting the waypoint to 1 and mess up the entire route. It’s a pain to have to go into the trip settings and drag what was supposed to be waypoint 9 from the #1 spot to the #9 spot where it’s supposed to be. 

I like there’s an option to set waypoints to go off grid, but once again, the app is very finicky when setting these waypoints, and it’ll often mess up the numbering sequence. 

I’d be willing to pay money for the premium plan, but your app can’t even set simple waypoints in order from start to finish without messing up. I don’t want it to automatically try to shorten the route. I want to go where I tell it to. Such a simple thing. I will be looking at other apps.
title: Don’t spend your money

text:
iPhone app is basically useless for route planning.. The app is focused on social networking features, not route planning. The social features are the landing page and the routes you are working on are buried in your profile. when you find the routes you are working on, the editing functions on the iPhone app are buggy and poorly organized for task. Everything looks pretty enough so they had a graphic arts pro working on this, but nobody tested the app by going through user tasks like changing the starting and ending points of the route, which is totally broken. Numerous small glitches, like hamburger menus (three bar icons that indicate a menu) that don’t do anything next to the waypoint list (if you can find it, it’ll take a few minutes).

Many little features show lack of consideration for users. If you tap feedback, thinking this will give you a chance to lodge a bug report, it only opens up an gas page — clearly indicating they are not interested in receiving bug reports, which would help both them and the user.

Maybe this is better on Android — I don’t remember it being so bad there. Or maybe it is this latest version. But I’d avoid the iPhone app for route planning. It’s badly designed for that purpose and very buggy. It may be fine for following other people’s routes and doing social media stuff about your ride.
title: iPhone app is basically useless for route planning.

text:
Not easy to plan route. I started the premium subscription a few days ago because I’ve heard great things about Komoot. However, I’m disappointed with its unintuitive interface so far.

I tried planning a route and wanted to return to the same path I had sent. Unfortunately, it tried to redirect me to a different route. I had to manually adjust the points to match my desired path.

It would be great if Komoot could incorporate natural language commands for route planning. I haven’t noticed this feature yet.

I also attempted to plan a long-distance walk, but the estimated completion time was discouraging. It seemed to assume that I was slow based on my activity level. I believe this is because Komoot doesn’t have access to my personal fitness data.

It would be beneficial if Komoot could allow me to input my fitness level, such as my biking, walking, and running speeds. This way, it could provide a more accurate estimate tailored to my abilities rather than relying on a generic baseline.

I understand that Komoot may not have access to my personal fitness data since I’m new to the app and haven’t used it for walks yet. However, I hope that Komoot will eventually incorporate this feature.

I’m glad I’m still trying out Komoot and haven’t made any financial commitments yet.

text:
Occasionally life-threatening routing. One hand: user-designed / vetted routes are generally superb. App is great for showing a rider new places to ride, and telling you what conditions (surfaces, grades) to expect. 

Other hand: sometimes (unpredictably) the routing software makes an edit that could get you killed. It has sent me on pieces of CA-1 in Pacifica that were 6 lane highway with frequent interstate on-ramp / exit-ramp crossings, which can be lethal. It had me cross 4 lanes of high speed CA-17 outside Santa Cruz (no traffic light) and then up 2+ miles of same next to 55 mph heavy car traffic & with little or no shoulder. Suicidal. Hated and feared every second of both. Terror. 

Software uses OpenStreets, and the routing never broke traffic law in my experience. But it led me to junctures where my choice was “retrace course back 10 miles” or “briefly take life into hands.” Cycling routing software should never do this. Should stress: these things happened all on Komoot 5-star-rated routes. 

Google Maps Cycling layer will route you onto goat paths and worse, but it’s great about not getting you killed. Komoot, for its part, won’t strand you on a rocky fire road or an overgrown path, but it WILL occasionally (& unpredictably) put you six unprotected inches from heavy traffic. Pick your poison. Use with care.
title: Occasionally life-threatening routing

Couple of points to consider. First, if you are on a hike and decide to turn back for any reason you need to stop the hike you are currently on, and program a new hike beginning at your current location and ending at your starting location.  To me, this is a huge safety flaw as returning to start point is likely to be your first choice when something goes wrong during your hike (injury, unexpected conditions on the trail, unexpected weather changes, etc.).  This should be an easy to use feature with one button or easy-to-find screen option.  In short, the app is great for planning a hike, but not so great at keeping you safe if things change. 

Second, on the Apple series watches it is difficult to toggle between the map-screen and the cue-sheet as the icons are small with a confusing layout.  (No direct toggle). Apparently, it’s easier on the Apple Watch Ultra as that watch has a function button that can be programmed to do this.

text:
Superb. Best app for trail runners.. I’ve been using Footpath for almost three years now. I found it originally from looking for the best app to sync truly offline maps to Apple Watch, ie no iPhone required. Since then I’ve used it to map routes in: UK, France, Germany, Portugal, Switzerland, Belgium, Italy, Austria, Norway, California, Japan and Finland. There is always a map that’s relevant to the region, it is always up to date, and it always works without fault. I’m currently in Madeira - bang up to date and I’ve just plotted my run for this afternoon.

I’ve started to take it for granted. I’m sure there are good competitors for walking or hiking where you would have your phone with you (All Trails is the main competitor I’ve used, and I suppose Strava but for some reason I don’t consider it in the same bracket). But if you go trail running, and you want only take your watch and not your phone, Footpath cannot be beaten. It is outstanding.

For balance, to add a negative remark or two, I would say that when reviewing your sessions in Apple Fitness, it’s missing a few data points that are present when you use Apple Workouts. Minor stuff like what the ambient weather was at the time. And I don’t like how the voice route guide cuts in to audio (eg podcasts) so I set it to vibrate only on my watch when there’s a guidance point upcoming. And the little dance you have to do to send it to your watch, going to the cue list and sending, just odd - there should be an obvious button as in my opinion it’s a primary workflow. 

It’s a five star application. I can’t remember the last time I bothered to write a review but I really think Footpath sits in a class of one, and I realised if it went away, I’d genuinely not know what to replace it with.
title: Superb. Best app for trail runners.

Sometimes especially if walking in wooded area it will want to take you a longer route or a safer route. 
The notes of altitude are a god send if you want to avoid tough walks up hill. 
Being able to view your journey via satellite you can pick out nice areas to stop and rest a while 
Overall this app is my lifeline a tool to help anxiety and give me freedom to get out and relax. Used along side google maps for the bus stops and timetables a day week etc walking can be achieved with piece of mind. Just remember to take a back up battery if on a long journey as your phone is your map you’re tickets your money and camera and boy are there so many beautiful things to see along those paths you didn’t know existed. Enjoy your freedom from the stresses of the world and get out there.

text: Sans doute la meilleure app. Pour en avoir essayé des dizaines, c’est la seule qui a (presque) tout! Visualisation des cartes en 3D satellite pour bien se faire une idée du terrain que l’on va rencontrer, traçage hyper intuitif en survolant les routes et chemins d’un doigt, la trace se « colle » toute seule aux chemins existants survolés rapidement du doigt, et si elle ne trouve pas de chemin sous nos doigts alors qu’on voit parfois grâce à l’image satellite qu’il y a bien une trace de tracteur là où l’on souhaite passer, on peut toujours suspendre d’un clic l’aimant automatique et tracer vraiment au doigt l’itinéraire souhaité, et basculer du mode automatique au manuel aisément et aussi souvent qu’on le souhaite au cours d’un même traçage d’itinéraire. Bien sûr on peut exporter tout ça sous plein de formats(gpx et kml entre autre) et aussi importer des gpx enregistrés ailleurs. On peut avoir une vue d’ensemble de toutes les traces créées pour voir facilement les zones qui restent à explorer. Dommage que la 3D s’incline moins quand on fait un zoom rapproché (google earth garde des angles hyper prononcés même en zoomant au maximum, ça permet de se faire une meilleure idée des pentes) et qu’il n’existe pas encore de version CarPlay pour pouvoir suivre les traces créées en voiture ou en moto (mais l’export gpx vers d’autres app compatibles CarPlay résoudre ce pb). En résumé, super appli de planification de parcours off road !
title: Sans doute la meilleure app

text:
App is OK; Trial Period IS NOT. I’ve used the app to plan and track hikes in NJ & it generally works well.  When on a hiking trip to Glacier National Park.  Since there is VERY limited GPS coverage I’m Glacier, I signed up for the 7-day upgrade trial.

As feared, the app did not work well in the wilderness.  Downloaded maps were okay for general orientation, but without live location services their value was so-so.  When I returned from the trip, I decided to cancel the trial on day #7.

AllTrails sent an email that I will be billed $36 for the trial subscription, WHICH IS FOR ONE YEAR!  Clearly this is another example of “subscription abuse” by corporate America.  I disputed the charge with my cc company & supplied sign-up and cancel documentation.  They agreed and issued a refund.

BUYER BEWARE.  AllTrails is actively participating in the ‘bill every user dry by 1,000 financial cuts’ club.  The app is generally good.  Do they REALLY have to try and screw every potential user for an extra buck?

ADDENDA:  After the pathetic response, i.e., AllTrails does not control pricing at the Apple App Store, I decided to see if I’m an exception.  So, I read the one-star reviews.  How many times can AllTrails apologize for subscription difficulties?  That’s not an Apple or Android problem.  It’s indicative of willful corporate greed, so I downgraded my review from 3 stars to 2.  

I’m old enough to remember when product creators focused on building a better mousetrap and assuring their customers were happy and well-served.
Rest in peace.
title: App is OK; Trial Period IS NOT

C’est tout aussi agréable aussi de faire des itinéraires que je n’ai jamais eu l’habitude de faire, car mes chiens ont découvre des endroits qui ne connaissent pas réellement les difficultés sont différentes, et je connais que moi aussi cela me fait énormément de bien et beaucoup plaisir.

text:
Déception. Quelle déception, à aucun moment je ne payerais une application aussi médiocre!
Première rando, cela nous fait passé par une grand route sans bordure pour vélo ou même piéton . Route emprunté par des fou du volant! Trop loin pour faire demi tour, pas eu le choix de mettre nos vie en danger sur plusieurs kilomètre afin de rejoindre l’autre partie de la rando!

text:
Pas de guidage ! Le comble !. Comment en 2026 on peut proposer une app de randonnée… sans aucun guidage (ni notification ni vocale) même si ça devait faire partie d’une formule payante !?
Incroyable mais rédhibitoire ! 

L’app est pourtant très intuitive, et bien organisée. La carte n’est pas la meilleure (Komoot fait mieux).

Les données sur Apple Santé ne sont pas complètes (seul le temps est ajouté, pas la distance, ni les calories…).

Je m’attendais à mieux venant d’une app comme celle-ci.

Aussitôt installée aussitôt désinstallée !

text:
J’adore et je déteste. Superbe application globalement mais :
- l’enfer pour tenter d’importer un gpx dans l’appli ou sur le site web, lorsque je fais partager sur mon gpx toutes mes appli de trails apparaît sauf alltrails - alltrails ne crée pas de dossiers sur l’iPhone contrairement à d’autres appli pour stocker les gpx -j’ai beau mettre le fichier dans le dossier téléchargement du cloud pour tenter de l’importer manuellement via l’appli mais il n’apparaît pas…. L’enferrrrr pour quelque chose de basic.

Du coup lorsqu’on est sur le terrain et parfaitement sur le chemin, l’appli nous indique que l’on est hors route…

Appli Apple Watch qui ne veut pas se charger, j’ai les dernières Maj et l’Apple Watch ultra 3

text:
Je ne comprend pas. L’application a l’air top et a le potentiel d’une application qui mérite 4 étoiles voir 5. 
Mais pour ça, il faut une application qui fonctionne .. 
Le système avec la carte etc est très sympa, pouvoir voir les circuits et autre aussi. 
On peut même éditer son propre circuit. 

Par contre, un site internet inutilisable .. avec des pop up pour que tu installe l’application. N’ayant pas le choix, j’ai installé l’application, pour cette fois-ci devoir me connecter sinon je peux pas utiliser l’application .. 

Ensuite, l’application te demande d’essayer tel ou tel fonctionnalité en passant par l’offre premium payante.. 

Je ne peux pas consulter des photos des pics de montagnes sans que ça bug, le menu déroulant une fois un circuit sélectionné bug, et pars vers le haut.

Et tout ça avec un pressing intense qui commence sur le site internet qui le rend inutilisable sur téléphone. 

Dès que je trouve mon sentiers de randonnée, je désinstalle l’application sans hésiter. 
L’application a un potentiel mais la stratégie déployée .. non merci
title: Je ne comprend pas

David
